SMTO-HTTP-0056 — SMTO won't send sign-in details over this Gateway connection

GUID: 6f175363-b693-423f-9a0e-77cd65acc13b
Slug: http-gateway-transport-insecure
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The link between SMTO and the Gateway isn't protected well enough to carry your passwords or keys, so SMTO stopped before sending the web request. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and find the Gateway this task used. Check that it shows Connected, and look for a Secure badge or an Insecure legacy or Identity changed badge. SMTO only sends sign-in details over a Gateway connection that is encrypted and verified, and these badges show whether it is.
  2. If the Gateway shows Insecure legacy or Identity changed, or its address starts with http:// instead of https://, ask the person who set it up to switch it to a secure connection and reconnect it. Once the connection is secure and its identity is confirmed, SMTO can safely pass your sign-in details through it.
  3. When the Gateway is connected securely, ask the Agent to run the web request again. Nothing was sent the first time, so trying again after the fix is safe.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Connected over a secure connection and the web request returns a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't turn off certificate checks or accept a new Gateway identity you haven't confirmed; that could send your passwords to the wrong computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway's connection is not an authenticated, encrypted route (verified HTTPS for an inbound Gateway, or the pinned secure connection for an outbound one), so the Server refused to send HTTP credentials over it; this older error kind has no direct current producer and is normally superseded by Gateway dispatch and enrollment checks.

What this means

  • This retained insecure-Gateway-transport kind has no direct current HTTP producer; current Gateway dispatch and enrollment own transport admission. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • This retained insecure-Gateway-transport kind has no direct current HTTP producer; current Gateway dispatch and enrollment own transport admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual Gateway trust/transport admission result; this retained label alone does not prove credentials were sent or rejected.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway's record in Settings › Setup › Gateways: an inbound Gateway must use an https:// address with a certificate that verifies, and an outbound Gateway must connect over its pinned secure (wss://) channel. Fix the Gateway's TLS setup or re-enroll it through the supported flow, keeping certificate verification on and never accepting an unverified replacement identity.
  • Use the supported authenticated HTTPS or pinned outbound Gateway transport before supplying credentials. Keep TLS verification enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authenticated Gateway route passes its existing trust checks before private values are supplied.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
